title: Founding Codex Edition 1
summary: Chapter 0 — Founding Instrument. Internal publication. The jurisdiction of the Department.

revisions.note: Reset for contemporary issue. Text of Chapter 0 unaltered.

title: Operational Procedures
summary: Standing instructions for officers attending a recognised Excess Time Event.

revisions.note: Field log amended. Causes remain out of scope.

paras: This manual is issued under the authority of the Permanent Secretary. It is not guidance. It is instruction.
Officers will observe, record, protect and restore, in that order, unless protection requires an earlier act.
The Department administers consequences. It does not create causes. Officers will not offer an explanation for an event beyond the facts recorded.
Where coincidence is proposed as a complete account, the officer will note the proposal and continue the record.

title: Chronometer Programme
summary: Specification and civil oversight of public chronometers used in the measurement of drift.
paras: The Chronometer Programme exists so that drift may be measured against a published tolerance.
Instruments are not oracles. They do not predict. They measure relation.
Public demonstration is permitted. Interpretation is not.
Civilian contractors may maintain an instrument. They may not vary the published tolerance.

title: Information Governance
summary: How the Department holds personal data, including records of events that are not yet eligible for disclosure.
paras: The Department is a data controller. Some records describe hours that failed to arrive. Those records remain personal data.
A subject access request will be answered within the statutory period unless the record is of an event that has not yet become eligible.
Eligibility is a matter of date, not of convenience.
Nothing in this policy confers authority over the lawful passage of time itself.

title: Statistical Yearbook 2026
summary: Official statistics on recognised Excess Time Events in Wales and associated jurisdictions.
paras: In the year to 31 March 2026 the Department recognised 184 Excess Time Events in Wales. Four were assessed as more than local.
The overwhelming majority of citizens did not knowingly encounter an event.
Coincidence remains the most common first account offered to officers. It is recorded. It is not accepted as a complete explanation.
Tables are National Statistics pending assessment.

title: National Risk Register — Excess Time
summary: The Department’s contribution to the National Risk Register.
paras: Excess Time is assessed as a low-probability risk with localised effects in most instances.
The Department does not invite the public to prepare beyond ordinary household resilience.
Where an event produces demonstrable effects upon public life, local authorities remain the first responders for welfare. The Department attends to continuity.

title: Annual Report and Accounts 2026
summary: Laid before the Senedd. The Department’s work, spending and estate.
paras: The Department continued to observe, record, protect and restore.
Regional offices at Bristol, Manchester, Edinburgh and Belfast remain closed due to budget reductions. Cardiff is the headquarters. Abercrave is a field station with restricted hours.
The Codex was reset for contemporary issue. The text of Chapter 0 is unaltered.
Staff in post at 31 March: 146 full-time equivalent.

title: Annual Report and Accounts 2025
summary: Previous year’s report.
paras: Recognised events: 171. Restoration completed in 149 cases.
The Minister asked for a review of coincidence as a closing entry. The review found it insufficient.

title: Annual Report and Accounts 2024
summary: Report for 2023–24.
paras: The estate review recommended the closure of four regional offices. The closures took effect the following year.

title: Consultation: Excess Time (Wales) Regulations
summary: Consultation on draft regulations. Closes 23 October 2026.
paras: The Welsh Government invites views on draft regulations for the administration of Excess Time in Wales.
The regulations do not confer authority over the lawful passage of time itself.
Responses should be sent to consultations@det.gov.wales or by post to Cathays Park.

title: Circular: Regional office closures
summary: Notice to local authorities and partner bodies.
paras: Bristol, Manchester, Edinburgh and Belfast are closed due to budget reductions.
All enquiries transfer to Cardiff. Abercrave remains a field station. There is no public counter at Abercrave.

title: Temporal Welfare Policy
summary: Welfare where displacement has produced demonstrable effects.
paras: No person’s time shall be deemed surplus solely by reason of economic unproductivity.
Hours devoted to friendship remain hours. Hours devoted to mourning remain hours. Hours devoted to wandering remain hours. Hours devoted to wonder remain hours.
Support is offered to restore recoverable continuity. It is not a benefit for unused time.

title: Public guidance: if an afternoon is missing
summary: What to do. What not to do.
paras: If an afternoon has failed to arrive where it was expected, continue with your ordinary affairs where you can.
Do not attempt to recover the hours yourself.
Notify the Department on form DET-44 if the absence produces a demonstrable effect upon your household or work.
Most such events are localised, temporary and resolved without lasting consequence.

title: Schools: teaching temporal continuity
summary: Memorandum for maintained schools in Wales.
paras: The Department does not teach history. It does not regulate memory.
Schools may request a visit or a pack. Officers will not discuss causes.
Pupils should be told that the existence of the Department is not evidence that they are at unusual risk.

title: Working paper: Geometry of unplaced hours
summary: Institute for Temporal Studies. Not a statement of departmental policy.
paras: This paper describes a method for mapping hours that have a time and no agreed place.
It is issued for peer review. It is not operational instruction.
Structure first. Interpretation later.

title: Working paper: Coincidence as insufficient explanation
summary: Why coincidence is recorded and not accepted as a closing entry.
paras: For generations incidents were regarded as coincidence. The Department was established upon the observation that coincidence alone proved an insufficient explanation.
This paper restates that founding observation in contemporary method.

title: Field report: Cribarth night readings
summary: Restricted. Redacted public extract.
paras: Readings were taken three nights running. The tables disagreed.
No Excess Time Event was recognised. The disagreement is retained on the file.
The full report is withheld under section 31 pending a further series.

title: Field report: Cardiff dock displacement
summary: A localised event. Restored.
paras: A morning failed to arrive for a working group on the docks. The hours were recovered the same week.
No lasting consequence was found. The public assurance holds.

title: Instrument of Establishment, 1951
summary: The order establishing the Department.
paras: The Department of Excess Time is established as an executive department operating under ministerial authority.
Its responsibilities extend across Wales and, by agreement, associated jurisdictions of the United Kingdom.
The Founding Codex is the first internal publication.

title: Minute: Abercrave station, 1963
summary: Opening of the valley field station.
paras: A field station is to be kept in the Upper Swansea Valley. It will not be a public office.
The minute does not name a civilian partner. Later files do.

title: Draft: Excess Time (Wales) Regulations 2026
summary: Draft statutory instrument. Not in force.
paras: These Regulations make provision for the recognition of Excess Time Events in Wales and for the duties of local authorities where such events produce demonstrable effects.
Nothing in these Regulations is to be read as conferring authority over the lawful passage of time itself.

title: Freedom of information disclosure log 2026
summary: Disclosures made this year.
paras: The Department has answered 63 requests this year. Twelve were refused in full. Four were neither confirmed nor denied.
Requests for the unredacted Cribarth series remain outstanding.

title: Staff handbook (extract)
summary: Public extract of conditions and conduct.
paras: Officers will not discuss causes in public.
Officers will not accept hospitality from persons who claim to sell recovered hours.
The reference TTG-13 appears on departmental stationery. It is a catalogue mark. It is not a public service.

title: Estates: Cardiff relocation
summary: Relocation of the public counter within Cathays Park.
paras: The public counter moves to the east wing on 6 October 2026. Appointments are preferred.
The headquarters remains Cathays Park. The registered address is unchanged.

title: Community programmes framework
summary: How the Department works with communities.
paras: Programmes exist to reduce harm arising from temporal displacement wherever reasonably practicable.
They are not cultural funding. They are not a substitute for ordinary local services.

title: Schools memorandum
summary: Companion to DET-GUID-009.
paras: Headteachers should use form DET-33.
Visits last one hour. Officers will not take questions on 1951.

title: Instrument 13 research programme
summary: Updated programme. Civilian observation continues.
paras: Instrument 13 remains under civil oversight.
The machine does not predict. It measures relation.
A further annex will be issued if the tables agree. They have not.

title: Peer review protocol
summary: How Institute papers are reviewed.
paras: Working papers are reviewed before they may be cited in operational instruction.
Reviewers are asked for method, not belief.

title: Regional estate map notes
summary: Notes to accompany the public map.
paras: Open: Cardiff. Limited: Abercrave. Closed due to budget reductions: Bristol, Manchester, Edinburgh, Belfast.

title: Forms catalogue 2026
summary: The numbered forms of the Department.
paras: DET-01 Incident Report. DET-14 Recovered Hours Declaration. DET-22 Chronological Damage Claim. DET-44 Lost Afternoon Notification. DET-61 Memory Continuity Assessment. DET-78 Application for Research Access.
Further forms are listed on the Department’s website. Paper copies may be collected at Cardiff on counter days.

title: Ministerial statement, March 2026
summary: Oral statement to the Senedd.
paras: The Minister said that the public should continue with their ordinary affairs.
The Minister said that the Department administers consequences and does not create causes.

title: Spending review settlement 2026
summary: Resource and capital.
paras: Resource DEL is reduced. The estate reduction already taken is not reversed.
The Codex reprint is met from existing budgets.

title: Equality impact assessment 2026
summary: Assessment of the year’s operational changes.
paras: The guiding maxim is restated. No person’s time is deemed surplus solely by reason of economic unproductivity.
Office closures have a differential effect on those who cannot travel to Cardiff. Correspondence remains available.

title: Welsh language scheme
summary: The Department’s scheme under the Welsh Language Standards.
paras: The Department will issue public-facing material in Welsh and English.
The Founding Codex is an internal publication in English. Supporting guidance is bilingual.
Correspondence received in Welsh will be answered in Welsh.

title: Records retention schedule
summary: How long records are kept.
paras: Recognised Excess Time Event files are retained for 75 years.
Unrecognised reports are retained for 7 years.
Catalogue mark TTG-13 is retained with the file. It is not a disposal class.
